clue.text: One enters this dirty city, only to come back

parts.note: Bath is the spa city in Somerset, England

indicators.note: coming back means the word for only is read from right to left

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: Someone visits a grimy city and immediately heads home again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come back' turns BUT into TUB. The definition is playful: you get into it while dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: people climb into a bath to get clean when they are grubby.

clue.text: Trams will become smart after this support

definitions.text: Trams will become smart after this
definitions.meaning: reading the letters of trams from the back gives smart, so this process turns one word into the other
help or endorsement given to someone

explanation.surface: A transport promise: the trams will be spruced up once funding arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing as a noun is endorsement or assistance, the same as support.

clue.text: What one should do in tailor's — be audacious

definitions.text: What one should do in tailor's
definitions.meaning: at a tailor's you test a garment by putting it on
the idiom means to be cheeky and see what one can get away with

explanation.surface: Advice for a shop visit, with a dare tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means testing someone's limits cheekily, while literally it means donning clothes to check the fit.

clue.text: Teacher's exclamation of impatience for missing opening

parts.note: tut is the sound of clicking one's tongue in irritation

indicators.note: missing its opening means the first letter of the word for is dropped

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher's irritated noise when something is absent from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher or one who instructs a small group.

clue.text: Criminal can be cured? Not quite: one robs in the main

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter of cured is cut off

explanation.surface: A question of whether a lawbreaker can be reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims CURED to CURE; 'Criminal' rearranges CANBECURE. 'The main' is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate who plunders ships on the high seas, 'the main' being an old word for the ocean.

clue.text: Husband in game met by wounding remark? Nonsense

indicators.note: met by means the next piece joins on after the first
in means the husband's letter sits inside the game's letters

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies
a barb is a cutting, hurtful comment

explanation.surface: A husband at a match is hit with an insult and dismisses it as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense or meaningless chatter.

clue.text: Rake pins tail of long rat

indicators.note: pins means holds in place, so the rake's letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: a rake is a dissolute man, a roué

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A garden rake traps the end of a long-tailed rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is a scoundrel or untrustworthy person, a synonym in its slang sense.

clue.text: Brazen editor goes after United Nations with a hoax

indicators.note: goes after places the editor's letters at the end

parts.note: a sham is a fraud or pretence

explanation.surface: A shameless journalist pursues the UN over a fake story.
explanation.definitionFit: Being brazen means showing no shame at all, bold and without embarrassment.

clue.text: Harry married fan

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so the following word is disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Prince Harry got married, and someone is a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiast, someone who looks up to and adores another.

clue.text: Fish on line — it builds arm muscles

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a barbel is a freshwater fish with whiskers

explanation.surface: Something fishy on a line that bulks up your biceps.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight-lifting bar with discs on each end, used for strength training.

clue.text: Sob quietly and tremble — it's this crossword!

parts.note: to sob is to cry
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A solver weeps and shakes over a fiendish puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names the kind of puzzle being solved: the adjective describes this crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: This puzzle is the puzzling, clue-based sort whose clues hide meaning in wordplay.

clue.text: Strike by head of governors hurt school

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces stand next to each other
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to ram is to strike hard
to mar is to damage or spoil

explanation.surface: Governors go on strike and a school suffers.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammar school is a selective British secondary school, so the word alone can stand for one.

clue.text: Ravel — put in a grave next to the French church

indicators.note: next to places the pieces side by side

parts.note: to inter is to bury
la is French for the (feminine)
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The composer Ravel is buried beside a French church.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel looks like the French composer, but here it is the verb meaning to tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle threads together, which is to weave them over and under each other.

clue.text: Arab maybe right about stockings? On the contrary

indicators.note: about would put the right letter around the stockings
on the contrary reverses that, so the stockings go around the right letter

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or tights

explanation.surface: An Arab man may be right about some stockings, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' alone would wrap R round HOSE; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles, so HOSE wraps R.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab is a breed of horse, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Information concerned with style

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Facts about fashion or manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind of art, a style of writing or music.

clue.text: Impressive hospital department note showing where the shakes first occurred?

parts.note: epic means grand or impressive
ENT is ear, nose and throat
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A grand hospital ward note pinpoints where trembling began.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the ground point above an earthquake's origin, where the shaking starts.

clue.text: Passing me her pale pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are poor and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone passes and lends a pale woman some trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing means fleeting or short-lived, lasting only a brief time.

clue.text: Worker's holding top half of baby in sink

indicators.note: holding means the workers' letters wrap round the next piece

parts.note: hands are workers, so the possessive gives the plural

indicators.note: the top half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A labourer cradles a baby in a sink, half-submerged.
explanation.definitionFit: A small basin for washing the hands, typically in a bathroom: a type of sink.

clue.text: Tommy about to keep going

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is the nickname for a British private soldier
on means about, as in a talk on a topic

explanation.surface: A British infantryman is about to carry on.
explanation.definitionFit: To persevere doggedly despite difficulties, continuing as a soldier would.

clue.text: South — they're oddly following sailor's course

indicators.note: following means the odd letters come after the others

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Heading south, oddly following a seaman's route.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter is the first course of a meal, an appetiser.

clue.text: Time off that is left over? Yes

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the phrase that is left is read backwards

parts.note: ie is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is
sure is an informal yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether holiday is what remains, and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time, when one is not working.

clue.text: United over unknown god

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: tied means joined or united
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A united group rallies over an unidentified god.
explanation.definitionFit: A deity is a god or goddess, a divine being.

clue.text: In plant, oxygen creates huge fire

parts.note: a fern is a plant
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Oxygen inside a factory sparks a massive blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a large uncontrollable blaze.

clue.text: Female right to wear Tony's tight underwear

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written with its s

explanation.surface: A woman borrows Tony's snug-fitting smalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wear' only joins: F and R are mixed in with TONYS by 'tight', meaning drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand of men's briefs with an inverted-Y seam at the front, a kind of underwear.

clue.text: Put up with a bass (fish)

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
an ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Tolerating a bass, the fish kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to tolerate or endure it.

clue.text: Speaker woe for us, unfortunately — keeping Bercow initially

indicators.note: keeping means the rearranged letters hold the next piece
unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
initially picks the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: John Bercow, the former Commons Speaker, brings woe on us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges WOEFORUS into SUWOOFER, which holds B. Speaker looks like Bercow's old office but means a loudspeaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A subwoofer is a loudspeaker for very low bass frequencies.

clue.text: Box containing Eastern weapon

indicators.note: containing means the boxing word holds the next letter

parts.note: to spar is to box

explanation.surface: A crate holds an Oriental weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A spear is a long-shafted weapon with a pointed head.

clue.text: Attempt to remove clubs from chest

indicators.note: remove means the clubs letter is taken out

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox or chest
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Trying to lift some golf clubs out of a trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: An offer is an attempt or bid to do something, as in an offer to help.

clue.text: Renovated street around university — one might be in charge of all the property

definitions.text: one might be in charge of all the property

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the next one
renovated means rebuilt, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A redeveloped road by a campus, overseen by an estate manager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Renovated' turns STREET into TRSTEE, and 'around' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee holds and manages property on behalf of others.

clue.text: Flower from South America with fine leaf, practically

parts.note: SA is South America
F is the abbreviation for fine on pencils

indicators.note: practically means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a frond is a leaf of a fern or palm

explanation.surface: A bloom from South America with a delicate leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron comes from a crocus, a type of flower, and is also its name.

clue.text: Shy creature's eggs expensive, we hear

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: we hear means the word for costly is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: dear means costly

explanation.surface: Timid animal's eggs are pricey, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A small timid European deer, an example of a shy woodland animal.

clue.text: Roman emperor imprisoning five, getting us apprehensive

indicators.note: imprisoning means the emperor's letters enclose the next one

parts.note: Nero was emperor of Rome
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A Roman emperor locks up five people, alarming us.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous means anxious or worried, the same as apprehensive.
